full_judgment: 24. Sulaiman, CJ., in Gopinath Naik Vs. C.I.T. (1939) 21 I.T.R. 26 (F.B.) laid down that an enquiry made by the Income-tax Officer from the people of the locality after the proceedings under section 23(4) have started on which no notice has been given to the assessee, are illegal, and not authorised by section 23(3). In this decision it has been further laid down that the Income-tax Officer is entitled to act upon the assessment of the previous year, if no better evidence is forthcoming, even independently or any presumption of continuity. If the assessee fails to produce satisfactory evidence, he fails to displace the previous year's estimate which is certainly admissible against him. Therefore, the assessee must be informed about the materials proposed to be made the basis for the estimate. It is now well settled by judicial pronouncements, although there is nothing in the Income-tax Act itself requiring the assessing authority to disclose to the assessee the material on which he proposed to act or to refer to it in the order, but natural justice demands that he should draw the assessee's attention to it before making the order providing the assessee with an opportunity to meet the same. In a case where this basis requirements to make the assessment order judicious, has not been complied with, the assessment order becomes illegal.
